systems.name: AI sales team
systems.line: Seven agents run outbound, from research to booked call.
systems.problem: Outbound is research, writing, follow-up and inbox triage, and it stops the day the person doing it gets busy.
systems.outcome: Every lead is researched and scored, every email is written and reviewed by different models, and every reply is read and answered or handed to a person.

systems.name: AI support desk
systems.line: A triage agent, four specialists and a judge on every ticket.
systems.problem: Support answers the same questions all day, the hard tickets wait behind them, and nobody checks what was actually sent.
systems.outcome: Each ticket is triaged, answered by an agent that looks the facts up, judged by a second model, and audited overnight. Refunds follow a written policy and uncertain tickets reach a person with the facts attached.

systems.name: AI content studio
systems.line: Research to published article, voice-over and social posts.
systems.problem: Publishing well takes research, writing, fact-checking, optimising, recording and sharing, and one of them always slips.
systems.outcome: Agents research, write, fact-check and optimise each piece. A person approves it, then it is published, voiced and shared, and its results come back as next week's brief.

systems.name: AI back office
systems.line: Invoices, receipts and bank lines, read, matched and questioned.
systems.problem: Bookkeeping is typing what a document already says, then finding the one line that does not match.
systems.outcome: Documents are read by a model and checked by arithmetic, bank lines are matched, anomalies are raised, and finance can ask questions in Slack and get answers from the books.

systems.name: Lead intake
systems.line: An enquiry followed from the form to a booked call.
systems.problem: Enquiries arrive at any hour, sit in an inbox, and the good ones go cold before anyone replies.
systems.outcome: Every enquiry is answered in seconds, scored, filed in the CRM and followed up until it books or goes cold.

systems.name: Support agent
systems.line: Answers what it can, hands over what it cannot.
systems.problem: The same questions are answered by hand every day, and the hard ones wait behind them.
systems.outcome: Covered questions are answered from the help centre at once. Everything else reaches a person with the context already written.

systems.name: Content pipeline
systems.line: Topic to published article, with a person's approval in the middle.
systems.problem: Publishing regularly needs research, drafting, review and sharing, and one of them always slips.
systems.outcome: A researched draft is ready each morning. Nothing is published until a person approves it, and sharing follows by itself.

systems.name: Order operations
systems.line: An order followed from checkout to the customer's inbox.
systems.problem: Orders, stock and customer emails live in different tools and are kept in step by hand.
systems.outcome: Each order is recorded once, stock is taken, the customer is kept informed and abandoned carts are followed up.

systems.name: Payments
systems.line: Every payment recorded exactly once, and checked daily.
systems.problem: Payment webhooks arrive twice or not at all, and nobody notices the books are wrong until month end.
systems.outcome: A ledger that matches the processor, a daily proof that it does, and overdue invoices chased on a schedule.

systems.name: Community operations
systems.line: Welcoming, moderating and announcing on a Discord server.
systems.problem: A growing server needs someone awake at all hours to welcome people and remove scams.
systems.outcome: Members are onboarded, scams are removed in seconds, and moderators are only asked about the cases that need judgement.

systems.name: Ops digest
systems.line: The week's numbers on one screen, and an alert when one breaks.
systems.problem: The numbers exist in five tools and nobody has the hour it takes to gather them.
systems.outcome: One summary every Monday with week-on-week change, and an alert the moment a number crosses its line.

systems.name: Reliability kit
systems.line: What every other workflow leans on when something fails.
systems.problem: Automations fail silently: a webhook arrives twice, an API is down, a schedule stops.
systems.outcome: Failures are caught, alerted once, parked for replay and noticed even when the failure is that nothing ran.

workflows.name: AI sales team · Research, outreach and replies
workflows.summary: Seven agents run outbound end to end: research each new lead, score it, write and review every email, read the replies, propose meeting times and answer objections from the case studies. A person is asked whenever an agent is unsure.
tests: a good lead is researched, scored, added to HubSpot and started on a sequence
a personal email address is never qualified, whatever the model scored
when the research model is down, a person is asked and nothing is guessed
the same lead submitting twice starts one sequence
an email is written with a proof point, reviewed by a second model, sent and recorded
a rejected draft is rewritten once with the reviewer's notes, then sent
a promise the business does not make is caught in code even when both models approve
a sequence that has had its four emails is closed without a model call
an interested reply gets three calendar times and opens a deal
'unsubscribe' stops the sequence even when the classifier read it as interest
an objection the documents do not cover goes to a person, unanswered
mail from someone who is not a lead is left alone
the weekly report counts the funnel in code

story.title: A lead fills in the form
story.copy: Typeform sends it in. A lead already in a sequence is not started twice.

story.title: Facts are gathered first
story.copy: Clearbit looks up the person and SerpAPI finds recent company news. Either can fail without stopping the run; the dossier records what it could not find.

story.title: A research agent reads the dossier
story.copy: Claude writes the brief a salesperson would want: the company, the likely pains, and a specific hook. It is told to say when the dossier is thin instead of filling the gap.

story.title: A scoring agent, then the rules
story.copy: A second model scores the fit. Then code applies the rules it may not overrule: a personal address or a two-person company is not qualified, whatever the score.

story.title: Three ways forward
story.copy: Qualified leads go to HubSpot and start a sequence. The rest join the Mailchimp newsletter. Anything an agent could not finish goes to a person in Slack.

story.title: Every hour, the next email is due
story.copy: At most twenty an hour, one lead at a time. A sequence that has had its four touches is closed.

story.title: A writer agent drafts it
story.copy: Claude writes from the research and the earlier subject lines, and may search the case studies in Pinecone for one proof point it is allowed to cite.

story.title: A different model reviews it
story.copy: The reviewer did not write the email and is told not to be kind. Then code checks what neither model should be trusted on: length, unfilled placeholders, promises.

story.title: Approved emails are sent and recorded
story.copy: SendGrid sends it. The message is logged, the sequence moves on three days, and HubSpot gets a note.

story.title: One rewrite, then a person
story.copy: A rejected draft gets one revision with the reviewer's notes. If it still fails the checks, the sequence pauses and Slack is asked.

story.title: A lead replies
story.copy: Gmail brings the reply in. Mail from anyone who is not in a sequence is left alone.

story.title: A classifier reads what they want
story.copy: Interested, an objection, not now, stop, or an out-of-office. Low confidence means a person reads it, and the word 'unsubscribe' is honoured whatever the model thought.

story.title: Interested: a booking agent offers times
story.copy: It reads the calendar, offers three free slots, and replies in the thread. A deal opens in HubSpot and the owner is told.

story.title: An objection: answered from the documents
story.copy: The objection agent may only use what the Pinecone search returns. A confident answer is sent; an unsure one goes to a person with the lead's own words.

story.title: Not now, stop, or away
story.copy: Snoozed for a month, stopped for good and marked in HubSpot, or pushed back a week. No model writes anything for these.
nodes: Push the next touch a week

story.title: Monday: the funnel, counted
story.copy: Sent, replies, meetings and what is waiting on a person are counted in code. An agent writes three sentences about them for Slack.

workflows.name: AI support desk · Triage, specialists and a judge
workflows.summary: A triage agent routes each Zendesk ticket to a specialist agent that can read Shopify, Stripe or the knowledge base. A separate judge checks every answer before it is sent, refunds are decided by a written policy in code, and anything uncertain reaches a person with the facts already gathered.
tests: an order question is looked up in Shopify, judged and answered
legal language goes straight to a person and no specialist is asked
a small refund inside the policy is made in Stripe and added to the reply
a refund over the limit is never made by the agents
an answer the judge rejects is handed over with the unsent draft
a promise is caught in code even when the judge passes it
a technical question is answered from the knowledge base
with the models down, the ticket still reaches a person
the same ticket delivered twice is answered once
the nightly audit grades every refunded answer and names the poor ones
Monday's gaps are grouped and posted
a week with no handovers posts an all clear without a model call
an unhappy survey opens a follow-up with a draft for a person
a happy survey is only recorded

story.title: A ticket is opened
story.copy: Zendesk sends it in. A ticket seen before is not answered twice.

story.title: A triage agent reads it
story.copy: Topic, urgency, sentiment and language. It is told not to answer.

story.title: Some tickets always get a person
story.copy: Legal language, an angry customer, an enterprise account or another language: code sends these straight to the team, whatever the model thought.

story.title: The rest go to a specialist
story.copy: Four agents, each with only the tools its job needs.

story.title: Orders: it looks the order up
story.copy: The agent reads the order and the customer's history from Shopify and Supabase before it writes a word.

story.title: Billing: it reads the charge
story.copy: It can look at Stripe. It cannot refund: it can only say a refund was asked for.

story.title: Technical and general: from the documents
story.copy: Both search the knowledge base in Pinecone and must name the articles they used.

story.title: A refund is decided by a written policy
story.copy: Under 100, not a third refund, not already refunded. Inside the policy, Stripe refunds it with an idempotency key. Outside, a person decides.
nodes: Add the refund to the reply

story.title: A judge checks the answer
story.copy: A different model, which did not write the reply, checks every statement against the facts the specialist gathered.

story.title: Code makes the final call
story.copy: Low confidence, a rejected verdict, a promise, a card number or a judge that could not be reached all mean the same thing: do not send.

story.title: Sent, and logged
story.copy: The reply goes out through Zendesk and the answer is recorded for the nightly audit.

story.title: Or handed over with everything attached
story.copy: The team gets the reasons, the facts found and the unsent draft as a private note, so nobody starts from zero.

story.title: Tickets waiting on people are watched
story.copy: Every ten minutes, anything near or past its response time is raised once per stage.

story.title: Every night, the agents are audited
story.copy: Every answer that moved money and a sample of the rest are graded by a separate agent. Poor grades are named in Slack.

story.title: Every Monday, the gaps become a to-do list
story.copy: What the agents could not answer is grouped into themes, each with the article, tool or policy that would fix it.

story.title: An unhappy customer gets a person
story.copy: A low survey score opens a follow-up with a draft note. The agent writes the draft; a person decides what is sent.

workflows.name: AI content studio · Research to published, voiced and shared
workflows.summary: Seven agents take a topic from research to a fact-checked, optimised draft. A person approves it in Slack, then it is published to WordPress with a cover image and an ElevenLabs voice-over, shared to LinkedIn, X and Facebook, and its results in PostHog become next week's topics.
tests: a topic is researched, written, fact-checked, optimised and put to a person
a point that cites a source that does not exist is dropped before writing
an unsupported claim is edited out, and the draft says it was edited
when the edit leaves the claim in, the topic goes back and nothing is saved
a citation to a source that does not exist is caught even when the checker passes it
with too few sources the topic is returned without a model call
an empty queue does nothing
an approved draft is published, illustrated, voiced and shared to three networks
approving twice publishes once
a rejection publishes nothing and keeps the reason
sharing still happens with a plain post when the social model is down
a malformed decision is a 400
Friday's topics build on what was read and never repeat a title

story.title: One topic each weekday
story.copy: The next queued topic is claimed in Supabase with an update that only succeeds once, so two runs cannot draft the same piece.

story.title: Sources first
story.copy: SerpAPI gathers up to six sources and numbers them. With fewer than two, the topic is sent back instead of written from nothing.

story.title: A research agent finds the angle
story.copy: Each key point must name the source it rests on. Code then drops any point that cites a source that is not there.

story.title: An outline that does not repeat
story.copy: The outline agent searches the published articles in Pinecone first.

story.title: A writer agent drafts it
story.copy: It reads the house style guide from Pinecone and may make only the supported points, citing each by number.

story.title: A different model fact-checks it
story.copy: Every claim is listed and marked supported or not. A citation to a source that does not exist is caught in code.

story.title: One edit, then back for a brief
story.copy: An editor agent removes what was not supported. Code checks the removed claims are really gone. If not, the topic returns with the reason.

story.title: Optimised, saved, and put to a person
story.copy: An SEO agent writes the meta text; code cuts it to length. The draft waits in Supabase and Slack asks for a decision.

story.title: A person says yes or no
story.copy: The decision takes the draft only if it is still pending, so a second click publishes nothing.

story.title: Published, illustrated and voiced
story.copy: WordPress gets the article. OpenAI makes a cover image and ElevenLabs reads it aloud. Either can fail without unpublishing anything.

story.title: Shared, one network at a time
story.copy: A social agent writes three posts and code cuts each to its network's limit. LinkedIn, X and Facebook are posted one after another, and one failing does not stop the next.

story.title: Friday: what was actually read
story.copy: PostHog counts readers per article. A strategist agent proposes three topics that build on what worked, and code refuses any that repeat a title.

workflows.name: Lead intake · Capture and qualify
workflows.summary: Takes an enquiry from any form, rejects junk, ignores repeats, has a model score the fit, then files it in the CRM and sends the right first reply.
tests: a good enquiry reaches the CRM and gets a booking link
a poor fit gets the nurture email and no CRM record
a bad email is rejected with a 400
a bot filling the hidden field is rejected
the same enquiry twice is handled once
an unreadable model reply goes to a person
a CRM outage parks the lead

story.title: An enquiry arrives
story.copy: Any form can post here. Bad emails, empty messages and bots that fill the hidden field are turned away with a 400.

story.title: The form gets its answer first
story.copy: The visitor sees success in milliseconds. Everything slower happens after the response.

story.title: Repeats are ignored
story.copy: The same email on the same day is one enquiry, however many times the button was pressed.

story.title: A model scores the fit
story.copy: It returns a score and a reason. If its reply cannot be read, the lead goes to a person rather than being guessed at.

story.title: Three paths
story.copy: A fit goes to the CRM and gets a booking link. A poor fit gets a helpful email. Anything unclear is flagged for review.

story.title: Sales is told, and nothing is lost
story.copy: If the CRM is down after three tries, the lead is parked for replay instead of disappearing.

workflows.name: Lead intake · Follow up the unbooked
workflows.summary: Each morning, writes to qualified leads who have not booked. Three nudges, two days apart, then the lead is marked cold and left alone.
tests: nudges a lead that is due and counts it
leaves a lead contacted yesterday alone
marks a lead cold after three nudges
skips leads that already booked

story.title: Every weekday morning
story.copy: It reads the qualified leads who have not booked, and checks in with the heartbeat monitor.

story.title: Only the ones that are due
story.copy: Two days since the last contact. State lives in the datastore, so no workflow sits waiting for days.

story.title: A nudge, then it is recorded
story.copy: Each of the three emails is different. The count is written back straight away.

story.title: It knows when to stop
story.copy: After three, the lead is marked cold and never written to again.

workflows.name: Lead intake · Booking sync
workflows.summary: When a call is booked, moves the lead forward everywhere at once: the lead record, the CRM deal and the sales channel.
tests: a booking marks the lead and opens a deal
a booking from a stranger is flagged
a resent webhook is handled once

story.title: The calendar reports a booking
story.copy: Calendar tools resend webhooks, so the booking id is checked first.

story.title: The lead moves forward
story.copy: The lead is marked booked, which is also what stops the follow-up emails.

story.title: The CRM and the team catch up
story.copy: A deal opens at the right stage and sales sees it in the channel.

story.title: Strangers are flagged
story.copy: A booking from someone who never enquired still gets noticed.

workflows.name: Support agent · Answer or hand over
workflows.summary: Answers a customer's message from the help centre when it is confident, and hands the conversation to a person with a summary when it is not.
tests: answers a covered question
hands over what the help centre does not cover
hands over an upset customer even when the answer is known
hands over when the model is unavailable

story.title: A customer writes in
story.copy: The helpdesk sends every message here. The agent's own replies and repeats are dropped.

story.title: It looks things up first
story.copy: The help centre is searched and the best four articles become the only thing the model may answer from.

story.title: It drafts, with a confidence
story.copy: The model returns an answer, its sources and whether a person should take over.

story.title: Confident: it replies
story.copy: Above the threshold, the answer goes to the customer.

story.title: Not confident: a person takes over
story.copy: The conversation is assigned with a private note, so nobody has to ask the customer to repeat themselves.

story.title: Every outcome is logged
story.copy: Answered or handed over, it is recorded. That log is what the weekly gap report reads.

workflows.name: Support agent · Ticket triage
workflows.summary: Labels each new ticket by topic and urgency, routes it to the right team, and pages someone only when it is urgent.
tests: a billing ticket goes to billing without paging
an urgent outage pages on-call
spam is closed and nobody is paged
an unreadable model reply falls back to the general queue for review

story.title: A ticket is opened
story.copy: Subject and body are read. Nothing else about the customer is sent to the model.

story.title: A model labels it
story.copy: Topic, urgency and sentiment. If the reply cannot be read, the ticket goes to the general queue marked for review.

story.title: It lands with the right team
story.copy: Spam is closed. Billing, engineering and general each get their own queue.

story.title: Only urgent tickets page someone
story.copy: Everything else waits its turn in the queue.

workflows.name: Support agent · Weekly gap report
workflows.summary: Every Monday, reads what the agent could not answer last week and tells the team which help articles are missing.
tests: reports the gaps
says all clear when nothing was handed over

story.title: Monday morning
story.copy: It reads last week's log for conversations that went to a person.

story.title: Questions become topics
story.copy: A model groups them and names the article that is missing for each.

story.title: The team gets a to-do list
story.copy: The report lands in the support channel. A clean week gets a short all-clear.

workflows.name: Content pipeline · Research and draft
workflows.summary: Takes the next topic off the list, researches it, drafts the article, and asks a person to approve it. Nothing is published from here.
tests: drafts the queued topic and asks for approval

story.title: One topic a day
story.copy: The next queued topic is claimed, so two runs can never draft the same one.

story.title: Research before writing
story.copy: A search gathers sources. The model is told to use only what is in them.

story.title: Outline, then a check
story.copy: A thin or unreadable outline sends the topic back for a better brief instead of producing a weak article.

story.title: The draft is written and saved
story.copy: It is stored as awaiting approval, with its sources.

story.title: A person decides
story.copy: The content channel gets approve and reject buttons. Publishing is a separate workflow that only a person can start.

workflows.name: Content pipeline · Approve and publish
workflows.summary: Receives a person's decision on a draft. Approved drafts are published to the CMS once and queued for sharing; rejected ones go back with the reason.
tests: approval publishes and records who approved
rejection publishes nothing and keeps the reason
approving twice publishes once
an unknown draft is refused
a malformed decision is a 400

story.title: A person presses a button
story.copy: Approve or reject, with who decided.

story.title: The draft must still be pending
story.copy: A second click, or a click on an old message, gets a 409 and publishes nothing.

story.title: Approved: published once
story.copy: The article goes to the CMS and the draft records who approved it and when.

story.title: Rejected: kept with the reason
story.copy: Nothing is deleted, so the reason is there for the next attempt.

workflows.name: Content pipeline · Share what was published
workflows.summary: Every hour, writes a post per network for anything newly published and schedules it. One network failing does not stop the others.
tests: schedules three posts and marks the article shared
uses a plain post when the model is down
does nothing when nothing is new

story.title: It looks for new articles
story.copy: Published and not yet shared. The flag in the datastore is the only state.

story.title: A post for each network
story.copy: The model writes three versions. If it fails, a plain title-and-link post is used instead.

story.title: Scheduled, then marked
story.copy: Each network is scheduled on its own, so one outage costs one post and not all three.

workflows.name: Order ops · New order
workflows.summary: Takes a new order from the store, records it once, takes its items out of stock, confirms to the customer, and warns the team about anything running low.

story.title: The store reports an order
story.copy: The request must carry the shared secret. Anything else gets a 401 and goes no further.

story.title: It is recorded once
story.copy: Stores resend webhooks when they are unsure. The order id is claimed first, so stock is never taken twice.

story.title: The customer hears straight away
story.copy: The confirmation does not wait for the stock work.

story.title: Each line comes out of stock
story.copy: One call per line item, retried three times.

story.title: Low stock is noticed at the moment it happens
story.copy: Anything at five or fewer becomes one message to the team.

story.title: A stock failure is parked

workflows.name: Payments · Event ledger
workflows.summary: Records each payment, failure and refund from the processor exactly once, updates the invoice, and sends the receipt or the retry notice.
tests: a payment is credited, the invoice paid and a receipt sent
the same event twice is one ledger line
a refund is a negative line and finance is told
a failed payment marks the invoice and asks for a new card
an unsigned request is refused

story.title: The processor reports an event
story.copy: Unsigned requests are refused. The reply is only sent once the event is safely recorded, so the processor retries anything that was not.

story.title: Exactly once
story.copy: Processors promise at-least-once delivery. The event id is claimed first, so a repeat changes nothing.

story.title: A payment
story.copy: Credited to the ledger, the invoice marked paid, a receipt sent.

story.title: A failure
story.copy: The invoice is marked and the customer is asked to update their card.

story.title: A refund
story.copy: A negative ledger line, and finance is told.

story.title: The processor gets its answer
story.copy: Events the business does not act on are acknowledged and ignored.

workflows.name: Payments · Daily reconciliation
workflows.summary: Each morning, compares yesterday's charges at the processor with the ledger and reports anything on one side and not the other.
tests: matching books post an all clear
a charge missing from the ledger is raised
a different amount is raised
a ledger line with no charge is raised

story.title: Two lists of yesterday
story.copy: What the processor says it charged, and what the ledger says was recorded.

story.title: Compared line by line
story.copy: Three things can be wrong: missing from the ledger, missing at the processor, or a different amount.

story.title: A clean day says so
story.copy: Finance gets a one-line confirmation, which is also proof the check ran.

story.title: A mismatch is recorded and raised
story.copy: Each issue is stored as open, then finance gets one critical alert naming them.

story.title: It checks in
story.copy: If this ever stops running, the heartbeat monitor notices.

workflows.name: Payments · Overdue reminders
workflows.summary: Each morning, reminds customers with overdue invoices at 3, 7 and 14 days, then hands the invoice to a person at 21.
tests: an invoice 8 days overdue gets the 7-day reminder
a step already sent is not sent again

story.title: It works out the step

story.title: A reminder, recorded

story.title: At 21 days a person takes over

tests: a scam link is removed, logged and reported

story.copy: Allow, review or remove, with a reason. Criticism is explicitly allowed.

story.title: Clear scams are removed
story.copy: The message is deleted, the author is timed out for an hour, and the action is logged with the original text.

story.title: Anything unsure goes to people
story.copy: That includes every message judged while the model is down. The automation never removes on a guess.

story.title: Everything else is left alone
story.copy: Which is most messages.

workflows.name: Community ops · Scheduled announcements

tests: a due announcement is posted once and marked sent
a future announcement waits
a failed post is marked and reported

story.title: Every five minutes
story.copy: It asks for announcements whose time has come.

story.title: Each one is claimed first
story.copy: The status moves from scheduled to sending in one update that only succeeds once, so overlapping runs cannot double post.

story.title: Posted and marked
story.copy: Sent announcements keep the time they actually went out.

story.title: A failure is visible
story.copy: It is marked failed and the team is told, instead of silently retrying an hour late.

workflows.name: Ops digest · Weekly summary

tests: compares this week with last and sends both ways
names a source that did not answer and still sends
sends the numbers even when the model is down

story.title: Four sources, two weeks
story.copy: Leads, orders, support and site traffic. Each is allowed to fail on its own.

story.title: The arithmetic is done in code
story.copy: This week against last week, per number. The model is never asked to count.

story.title: A model writes four sentences
story.copy: It sees only the finished numbers and is told not to invent causes.

story.title: It says what is missing
story.copy: A source that did not answer is named in the digest, not silently left out.

story.title: Channel, inbox, heartbeat
story.copy: Posted, emailed, and checked in so a missed Monday is noticed.

workflows.name: Ops digest · Threshold alerts
workflows.summary: Checks each watched number hourly and alerts when it crosses its line, and again when it recovers. It does not repeat itself in between.
tests: alerts when a number crosses its line
stays quiet while it is still breached
says when it recovers

story.title: Each number has a line
story.copy: A value, a threshold and a direction, kept in one table anyone can edit.

story.title: Only a change of state matters
story.copy: Breached an hour ago and still breached is not news.

story.title: One alert in, one alert out
story.copy: The team hears when it breaks and when it recovers, and nothing in between.

workflows.name: Reliability · Error handler
workflows.summary: Catches a failure in any workflow, logs it to Supabase, and alerts Slack once per distinct error per hour so a broken loop cannot flood the channel.
tests: a new failure is logged and alerted
the same failure inside the hour is not alerted twice
an alert still goes when the log is down

story.title: A workflow fails
story.copy: Every workflow in the library names this one as its error workflow, so a failure anywhere arrives here.

story.title: It is logged once
story.copy: The error is written to Supabase with a fingerprint of workflow, node, message and hour. A unique constraint refuses a repeat inside the hour.

story.title: Slack hears about it once
story.copy: Only a new fingerprint posts an alert, so a loop failing a thousand times is one message. If the log itself is down, the alert still goes.

workflows.name: Reliability · Idempotency guard
workflows.summary: Answers one question for a caller: has this event been handled before? Webhooks are delivered more than once; a unique key in Supabase is what makes that safe.
tests: a first event is not a duplicate
a repeat is a duplicate
a database outage stops the caller and is not read as a duplicate

story.title: A caller asks
story.copy: It passes a scope and a key: an order id, a payment event id, a lead's email.

story.title: The key is claimed in Supabase
story.copy: One insert against a unique constraint. The database decides, so two runs at the same moment cannot both win.

story.title: A refused insert is read carefully
story.copy: Refused because the key exists means duplicate. Refused for any other reason stops the caller: an outage is never mistaken for 'already handled'.

workflows.name: Reliability · Notify
workflows.summary: The one place alerts leave from. Posts to Slack, and falls back to a SendGrid email when Slack is down, so an outage cannot hide its own alert.
tests: posts to Slack
falls back to email when Slack stays down
recovers when Slack fails once

story.title: Something needs saying
story.copy: Any workflow calls this with a text and a level. No other workflow talks to Slack for alerts.

story.title: Slack first
story.copy: Three attempts, a second apart.

story.title: SendGrid if Slack is down
story.copy: A failure after the retries takes the second output and the alert still arrives, by email.

workflows.name: Reliability · Dead letter
workflows.summary: Keeps the payload of work that could not be finished in Supabase, with the reason, so nothing is lost when a platform is down.
tests: parks the payload as pending
still parks when Slack cannot be reached

story.title: Work could not be finished
story.copy: A caller hands over the payload, where it came from and why it failed.

story.title: It is parked, not dropped
story.copy: The payload is stored in Supabase as pending, with the address that can replay it.

story.title: Slack is told
story.copy: The alert is best effort: parking has already succeeded.

workflows.name: Reliability · Dead letter replay

tests: replays pending items and marks them
abandons after the fifth failure and escalates
does nothing when nothing is parked

story.title: On a timer
story.copy: Every fifteen minutes it asks Supabase for parked work.

story.title: One at a time
story.copy: Each item is sent back to the address that can redo it. One slow item does not hold the others.

story.title: Five attempts, then a person
story.copy: A failed replay is counted. At five the item is abandoned and escalated in Slack.

workflows.name: Reliability · Heartbeat monitor

story.copy: Nothing overdue means nothing is sent.

workflows.name: Content · Industry news digest

refuses an empty feed

story.title: The people who must act are told

workflows.name: Calendar · Morning agenda

stays silent on an empty day

story.title: One message, or none

workflows.name: Monitoring · Uptime checks
